labels.name: status:in-progress
labels.description: The issue is being worked on

items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The `proxmox_virtual_environment_file` resource requires SSH access to the node when creating and uploading a cloud-init snippet.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like to reduce usage of SSH for provisioning resources, thus I propose to use the https://github.com/kdomanski/iso9660 library to create an ISO image on the fly (basically what's happening here: https://github.com/Telmate/terraform-provider-proxmox/blob/186ec3f23bf4a62fcad35f6292fa1350b8e1183b/proxmox/resource_cloud_init_disk.go#L77-L122)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The information:
> Consider using `proxmox_virtual_environment_download_file` resource instead. [...]

On the `proxmox_virtual_environment_file` docs is good advice for downloading OS installer ISOs directly onto the node, but for cloud-init disks you usually would want to create them locally from a yaml file or inline specification.

**Additional context**
I'm happy to create a pull request for this feature, if desirable.

items.body:
This is an "umbrella" ticket (call it an epic, or whatever) to track the migration of the `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm` resource to the [Plugin Framework](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/framework).

#### Motivation
Check out the [benefits of Plugin Framework](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/framework-benefits) from HashiCorp. There are quite a lot.

Specific to this provider:

- The Plugin Framework gives [better control](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/framework-benefits#control-over-built-in-behaviors) over `Optional` and `Computed` fields and their *defaults*, which is extremely useful in handling the `clone` operation. During cloning, we inject lots of attributes from a template that are not present in the clone while also overwriting some of the template parameters from the clone.

  Related:
  - #103
  - #247
  - #360
  - #566
  - #718
  - #781 
  - #850
  - #873
  - #1106
  - #1219
  - #1224
  - #1299
  - #1304
  - and others

- Ability to manage data transformations via custom data types (various conventions for lists/sets in the Proxmox API).

- Better support for collection data types (lists, and specifically sets, to handle unordered collections of items).

#### Challenges
- There's a vast amount of functionality to port, and some (or most?) of it needs to be re-implemented to leverage the benefits of the Provider Framework data model/custom types.

- Severe lack of the provider's code test coverage. The changes/re-implementation will introduce new bugs that will be hard to catch.

#### Compatibility
Inevitably, some attribute formats and semantics will be incompatible with the old version. Also, some attributes will be renamed/removed. Known incompatibilities are marked with :exclamation: below.


#### Implementation

The `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm2` resource contains the new implementation.  

Status of features/attributes:

items.body:
**Describe the bug**

Using the resource `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm` and creating a `user_data` file using `proxmox_virtual_environment_file` resource and using `migrate=true` on the VM when changing the node, the VM is deleted/added instead of changed.

Why I wish to do it this way is to inject per VM specific variables to user_data (cloud-init). Currently I cannot do that if I wish to retain the migrate logic between nodes. Eg `migrate=true`

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create a resource 'environment_file' and 'vm'
2. Modify the resource 'vm' to use another host (E.G Migrate the host from one node to another). (Nothing else is changed.)
3. Run 'tofu plan'
4. See that it wants to destroy instead of migrate.

Please also provide a minimal Terraform configuration that reproduces the issue.

  expire: false

users = [

Changing the property `initialization.user_account.keys` causes a VM resource to be re-created. This also means losing data.

**Steps to reproduce the behavior**

1. Create a resource `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm` with property `initialization.user_account.keys` set to an array of strings.
2. Run `terraform apply`: The resource is created successfully.
3. Change one of the strings in the array of the property `initialization.user_account.keys`.
4. Run `terraform plan`: The resource would be recreated (destroyed and created again, which means losing data)

Changing the property `initialization.user_account.keys` should not destroy the resource because the SSH keys are applied by _cloud-init_ only at the first boot anyway. In other words, the property can be safely ignored after the initial creation of the resource.

Why would anyone then change this property? It is often practical to not assign literal strings to this property, but a variable which is shared across resources. In other words, a set of SSH keys is maintained in one location (e.g. vars.tf) and then reused in multiple resources to avoid duplication of string literals.

items.title: Support in-place Cloud-Init password update
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

I understand the general philosophy that Terraform is primarily for Day-0 provisioning, and Day-1 management should ideally be handled by Configuration Management tools. However, simply rotating or updating a VM's password is a basic administrative task that shouldn't strictly require a full Configuration Management stack similar to how SSH keys can be updated without one.

Currently, updating the password in the `initialization` block doesn't apply smoothly in-place. I am aware of the underlying challenge: the Proxmox API does not return the current Cloud-Init password, making it impossible for Terraform to know the actual remote state.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Since the remote state is unknown, Terraform could rely on its local state.
If the password in the `.tf` configuration differs from the local `.tfstate`, the provider should trigger an in-place update of the Cloud-Init drive. This perfectly mimics the Proxmox Web GUI behavior: you can input a new password without knowing the old one, and it simply regenerates the Cloud-Init drive with the new credentials.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Alternatively, introducing an environment variable or a module parameter (e.g., `force_password_update = true`) to explicitly force this in-place generation would also solve the issue cleanly.

**Additional context**

I know this can technically be achieved using custom Cloud-Init snippets via the `proxmox_virtual_environment_file` resource. However, this approach introduces unnecessary friction and complexity, especially given the known challenges and limitations with the Proxmox API regarding snippet file uploads.

A native, straightforward way to update the password in-place via the initialization block would greatly improve the UX. 

Thanks for considering this.

items.title: Removing an ip_config block does not delete ipconfigN from the VM (plan never converges, VM reboots on every apply)

labels.name: status:in-progress
labels.description: The issue is being worked on

items.body:
### Describe the bug

Removing an `ip_config` block from `initialization` is planned as a removal and reported as applied, but the corresponding `ipconfigN` key is never deleted on the Proxmox side. The next plan shows the exact same diff again, forever.

Because applying the change also stops and starts the VM, every apply reboots the guest and achieves nothing.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a VM with two `ip_config` blocks (two network interfaces):

```hcl
initialization {
  datastore_id = "..."
  ip_config {
    ipv4 {
      address = "10.0.0.10/24"
      gateway = "10.0.0.254"
    }
  }
  ip_config {
    ipv4 {
      address = "10.1.0.10/24"
    }
  }
}
```

2. `terraform apply`
3. Remove the **second** `ip_config` block from the configuration.
4. `terraform apply` — the plan shows:

```
~ initialization {
    - ip_config {
        - ipv4 {
            - address = "10.1.0.10/24" -> null
          }
      }
  }

Plan: 0 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy.
```

and the apply succeeds:

```
Apply complete! Resources: 0 added, 1 changed, 0 destroyed.
```

5. On the PVE node:

```
# qm config <vmid> | grep ipconfig
ipconfig0: gw=10.0.0.254,ip=10.0.0.10/24
ipconfig1: ip=10.1.0.10/24        # still there
```

6. `terraform plan` — same diff as in step 4, indefinitely.

### Expected behavior

Dropping an `ip_config` block should send `delete=ipconfig1` in the update call, so the key is removed from the VM configuration and the next plan is clean.

### Actual behavior

`ipconfigN` stays in the VM configuration. State and plan never converge. Each apply additionally power-cycles the VM (cloud-init changes are applied by stopping and starting it), so the guest is rebooted repeatedly for a change that is never made.

### Notes

`vmGetCloudInitConfig(d)` builds the cloud-init config from what is *present* in the configuration, and the update path assigns it to `updateBody.CloudInitConfig`. Keys that disappeared from the configuration are not added to the delete list — unlike, for example, `netN` or `serialN`, which do get `del = append(del, ...)` treatment elsewhere in the same update function.

This looks like the same root cause as #2259 (removing a network device does not remove it from Proxmox).

### Workaround

Remove the key manually on the node, then the plan is clean and stays clean:

```
qm set <vmid> --delete ipconfig1
```

This does not disturb a running VM — the guest keeps running and cloud-init picks up the new configuration on its next boot.

### Environment

- Provider: `bpg/proxmox` v0.111.1 (latest at the time of writing)
- Proxmox VE: 8.4.12
- OpenTofu 1.11
- Six VMs affected, all reproducing identically

items.title: Sequenced VM power control after guest-side operations (golden image / publish workflow)
items.body:
# Sequenced VM power control after guest-side operations (golden image / publish workflow)

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

When building golden images we often need this sequence in a **single** `terraform apply`:

1. Keep the VM **running** so we can SSH (or otherwise) into the guest for sanitize steps (`apt clean`, `cloud-init clean`, wipe `machine-id`, etc.).
2. Then **gracefully shut down** the VM.
3. Then **clone** it and set `template = true` (publish into a dedicated VMID range).

With `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm`, `started` is part of the same resource desired state. Terraform applies the full VM update **before** dependent resources run. So if `started = false` on publish, the guest becomes unreachable **before** guest provisioners / `terraform_data` remote-exec can run (`host for provisioner cannot be empty` once QEMU guest agent IPs disappear).

Workarounds today are awkward:

- Leave `started = true`, `poweroff` from inside the guest, then **poll** Proxmox (`pvesh` / `qm status`) until `stopped` before `clone` — extra SSH to the node, not declarative.
- Blind `time_sleep` after `poweroff` — fragile.
- Split into multiple applies / `-target` — bad for CI.

## Describe the solution you'd like

A **separate, sequenceable** way to manage power state (and ideally guest execution), for example:

1. A `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm_power` resource (name TBD), or equivalent action:
   - Arguments: `node_name`, `vm_id` (or resource reference), `state` (`running` | `stopped`), optional `shutdown_mode` (`acpi` / `hard`).
   - Can `depends_on` a guest sanitize step, and be depended on by a second VM that `clone`s the source.
2. Optionally **guest-agent exec** as a first-class resource (run commands via QEMU GA, then the power resource stops the VM) so SSH into the guest is not required.

Ideal publish graph:

```
vm (started=true) → guest_sanitize → vm_power(stopped) → vm_template (clone + template=true)
```

All in one apply, without node SSH helpers.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

1. Guest `poweroff` + external / `terraform_data` poll of QEMU status over SSH to the Proxmox node until `stopped`, then provider `clone` + `template = true`.
2. Fixed `time_sleep` after guest `poweroff` (unreliable).
3. Two-phase applies / `-target` (poor CI UX).
4. Setting `started = false` on the same VM resource during publish (breaks guest connectivity before sanitize).
5. Doing `qm clone` / `qm template` entirely via `remote-exec` on the node (works, but duplicates what the provider already supports and mixes shell with IaC).

## Additional context

- Provider: `bpg/proxmox` (`proxmox_virtual_environment_vm` with `clone` and `template = true`).
- Use case: golden image pipeline — build VM in a temporary VMID range, publish as template in another range; consumers select latest template with `max(vm_id)` among tags.
- Related pain: guest IPs from the agent are empty once the VM is stopped, so anything that needs SSH must run while the VM is still running on the hypervisor.
- Happy to refine the resource shape if you prefer Actions / lifecycle hooks over a standalone power resource.

items.title: vm: align cloud-init ip_config limit with network devices
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

The `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm` resource supports up to 32 `network_device` blocks, but `initialization.ip_config` is still limited to eight entries by a hardcoded `MaxItems: 8` in `proxmoxtf/resource/vm/vm.go`.

Issue #798 originally reported both limits. PR #822 raised the VM network-device limit to 32 and closed #798, but it did not update the matching cloud-init `ip_config` schema. VMs can therefore define more than eight interfaces but cannot assign provider-managed cloud-init IP configuration to interfaces 9–32.

**To Reproduce**

1. Configure a `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm` with at least nine `network_device` blocks.
2. Add a corresponding `initialization.ip_config` block for each device.
3. Run `terraform validate`, `tofu validate`, or plan the configuration.
4. Observe provider-side schema validation reject the ninth `ip_config` block:

```text
Error: Too many ip_config blocks

No more than 8 "ip_config" blocks are allowed
```

**Expected behavior**

`initialization.ip_config` should accept up to 32 entries, matching `network.MaxNetworkDevices` and the VM resource's supported interface count.

**Proposed solution**

- Define the initialization IP configuration limit in terms of `network.MaxNetworkDevices` rather than another independent literal.
- Update the VM resource documentation to state the 32-block limit.
- Add schema regression coverage with 32 `ip_config` blocks.
- Add an acceptance test for a VM with 32 network devices and matching cloud-init IP configurations.

This is a non-breaking schema relaxation; existing configurations are unaffected.

**Additional context**

items.title: Wait for VM startup using guest agent `exec` and `cloud-init status --wait`
items.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/bpg/terraform-provider-proxmox/discussions/389
Originally posted by **satwell** June 25, 2023 The PVE API [exposes](https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/api-viewer/#/nodes/{node}/qemu/{vmid}/agent/exec) QEMU Guest Agent's "exec" support, which lets you execute a command on the guest as root. Is there some sensible way that support for this could be added to the provider? Here's my use case. I'm using cloud-init for initial VM setup, but I'd like Terraform to wait until cloud-init has completed before considering creation complete. Cloud-init conveniently [provides a `cloud-init status --wait` command](https://cloudinit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/cli.html#cli-status) that will run until cloud-init is done. I could just use a `remote-exec` provisioner to connect to the VM and run that command. But that requires setting up an ssh connection to it. Which means the ssh port needs to be reachable, keys are set up, the the username matches what the cloud-init image uses, etc. It would be a lot cleaner if I could just use the guest agent for this. In an ideal world, the proxmox provider would be able to define a new provisioner for VM resources that would use the guest agent to run commands. But from my quick investigation, it doesn't sound like there's any way in Terraform to create new provisioner types. Are there other ways that would make sense to add support for the exec API? LIke an additional option in the vm resource type, or a new resource type? Or should I just find or write an external tool that uses the exec API and call it with a `local-exec` provisioner?

items.title: Snippet upload reports empty/ambiguous "error transferring file:" message
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

When an SSH-based file upload (e.g. `content_type = "snippets"`) fails, the provider reports:

```text
Error: error transferring file:
```

with **no detail after the colon**, making the failure impossible to diagnose.

Root cause: in `proxmox/ssh/client.go` (`uploadFile`), the error is built from the remote command's combined output only, and the actual Go error is discarded:

```go
output, err := sshSession.CombinedOutput(cmd)
if err != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("error transferring file: %s", string(output)) // err dropped
}
```

Whenever the failure produces no remote stdout/stderr — a non-zero exit with no output, an SSH session failure, or a local stdin-copy error (for example pointing `source_file.path` at a directory) — `output` is empty and the user sees a blank reason. The underlying `err` (e.g. `Process exited with status 1`, `read ...: is a directory`) is lost.

Reported in discussion #2954.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Configure a `proxmox_virtual_environment_file` with `content_type = "snippets"` whose upload fails (e.g. `source_file.path` points at a directory, or the remote write fails silently).
2. Run `terraform apply`.
3. See `Error: error transferring file:` with no cause.

```hcl
resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_file" "cloud_init_user_default" {
  node_name    = "pve"
  content_type = "snippets"
  datastore_id = "local"
  source_file {
    path      = "./cloud-init/" # directory -> upload fails silently
    file_name = "user-data-default.yml"
  }
}
```

```text
Error: error transferring file:

  with proxmox_virtual_environment_file.cloud_init_user_default,
  on virtual-machines.tf line 20, in resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_file" "cloud_init_user_default":
  20: resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_file" "cloud_init_user_default" {
```

**Expected behavior**

The error message should include the underlying error so the cause is actionable.

**Additional context**

- Provider version: latest (main)
- Discussion: #2954

items.title: `proxmox_virtual_environment_file` snippet upload hangs from high-latency clients
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

When Terraform runs from a host with high network latency to the Proxmox node
(~140ms RTT in our case), creating `proxmox_virtual_environment_file` resources
with `content_type = "snippets"` regularly stalls and never completes. The apply
sits there and eventually we give up. Running the exact same configuration from a
host a few ms (<5ms) away from the node completes reliably in 0-2 seconds, every time.

So it looks latency-sensitive rather than config-related.

On the Proxmox node we occasionally see this in the sshd log around the time of a
stall:

```text
May 26 05:49:39 hypervisor-05 sshd[2000]: Timeout before authentication for connection from <client-ip> to <node-ip>, pid = 229989
```

Interestingly, while the apply appears to be stuck/retrying, we do not see new
`Timeout before authentication` lines piling up — it's quiet, as if the client
isn't actually re-dialing.

**To Reproduce**
1. Have terraform that creates 20 VM's each with their own cloud-init across 3 hypervisors.
2. Run Terraform from a host roughly 140ms away from the Proxmox node.
3. Apply a config that creates one or more snippet files (we use `for_each`).
4. The apply hangs and does not finish. 
5. Run the same config from a host close to the node — it completes in ~1-2s.

Note: Some VM's will create successfully but re-applying doesn't fix the issue because the provider seems to have failed badly and requires manual cleanup or manual imports which makes it difficult to automate against failures. Also, the apply hangs for over 5mins before we manually kill it as it gets stuck on retrying the "node_cloud_init" resource as shared below.

Minimal-ish config (we use private_key auth in the provider `ssh` block):

```hcl
resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_file" "node_cloud_init" {
  for_each     = toset([for i in range(0, var.node_count) : tostring(i)])
  content_type = "snippets"
  datastore_id = "local"
  node_name    = random_shuffle.available_nodes.result[tonumber(each.key) % length(random_shuffle.available_nodes.result)]

  source_raw {
    data = templatefile("${path.module}/cloudinit/cloud-init.yaml", {
      public_key = autoglue_ssh_key.ssh_key.public_key
      hostname   = "${var.role}-${var.name}-${each.key}"
    })
    file_name = "${var.cluster_name}-${var.role}-${var.name}-${each.key}-cloud-init.yaml"
  }
}
```

**Expected behavior**

Snippet upload should complete (or fail with a clear error) regardless of client
latency, the same way it does from a nearby host.

**Additional context**

I had a read through `proxmox/ssh/client.go` to understand the snippet upload path
and wanted to share what I found in case it helps — happy to be corrected:

- The upload `context` (built from `timeout_upload` in `fileCreate`) doesn't seem
  to reach the SSH layer. `connect()` uses `ssh.Dial("tcp", host, cfg)`, which
  doesn't take a context, and the `ssh.ClientConfig` instances don't set
  `Timeout`. There's also no keepalive on the connection. So if a handshake
  stalls, I don't think anything bounds it client-side until sshd's
  `LoginGraceTime` (default 120s) closes it — which lines up with the
  `Timeout before authentication` log.
- Each snippet upload looks like it opens two SSH connections: one in
  `NodeStreamUpload`, and a second one via the sudo-availability probe
  (`getSudoValue` → `getSudoAvailability` → `openNodeShell`). With `for_each` and
  Terraform's default parallelism that's a fair number of simultaneous half-open
  handshakes, and at 140ms each I suspect we're tripping sshd `MaxStartups`
  (default `10:30:100`), which starts dropping connections probabilistically. At
  low latency the handshakes finish fast enough that they never pile up, which
  would explain why it only reproduces from far away.
- The sudo-availability cache holds its write lock across the whole SSH round
  trip, so if that one probe connection stalls, every other in-flight upload
  seems to block on the mutex rather than re-dialing — which might explain why it
  looks like it's retrying but we don't see new sshd timeouts.

I didn't want to jump straight to a PR since there are a few possible directions
(wiring the context/timeout through and adding a keepalive, reusing the existing
connection for the sudo probe, adding retry/backoff around the dial, throttling
concurrent handshakes). Curious whether you've seen this before and how you'd
prefer to approach it. Glad to put up a PR once there's a direction you're happy
with.

---

- Single or clustered Proxmox: clustered
- Proxmox version: 9.2.2
- Provider version: 0.107.
- Terraform/OpenTofu version: 1.10.7
- OS (where you run Terraform/OpenTofu from): ubuntu/debian
- Debug logs (`TF_LOG=DEBUG terraform apply`): Can't easily share these details since it was a live environment but when it's happening all it says is that it's retrying. There wasn't any actionable debug output to share for that section of the DEBUG logs.

Proxmox has a ciupgrade boolean that defaults to 1 (appears as "Upgrade packages: Yes" in the Proxmox web UI) and this causes the VM's package manager to update packages on first boot.  https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/chapter-qm.html#_cloud_init_specific_options

I would like a boolean configuration option added to the proxmox_virtual_environment_vm initialization stanza to turn this setting off.

In my specific use case, the default value creates a race condition when using Ansible with Terraform where Ansible playbooks initially fail to update packages because the package manager cannot get a lock (I'm using Debian cloud images so this is the dpkg lock).  If I wait a few minutes and then run Terraform again, the Ansible playbooks will run successfully.

I'm using https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ansible/ansible/latest/docs for the Ansible provider but there may be other use cases where folks would like to change the default behavior.
